content: 1. Indication-Specific Dosing for Natural Progesterone: Natural progesterone is applied topically at a dose of 20 mg (equivalent to 1/4 teaspoon of cream) daily to the thighs or upper arms for 20 days each month. This regimen is used to manage vasomotor symptoms of menopause, osteoporosis, and premenstrual syndrome (PMS). Studies have shown positive results for menopausal vasomotor symptoms, while results for osteoporosis and PMS are mixed or negative. 2. Drug Interactions with Natural Progesterone: Apalutamide: Reduces the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Bosentan: Decreases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Bosutinib: Progesterone increases bosutinib levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Carbamazepine: Reduces progesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Clarithromycin: Increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat: Increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Enzalutamide: Decreases progesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fedratinib: Increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fosphenytoin: Decreases progesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib: Increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ivosidenib: Decreases progesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lonafarnib: Progesterone increases lonafarnib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lorlatinib: Decreases progesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Drugs Requiring Caution and Monitoring: Atazanavir, Ceritinib, Chloramphenicol, Conivaptan, Darunavir, and Ketoconazole: These drugs increase progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cenobamate: Decreases progesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Dabrafenib: Decreases progesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Danazol: Increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Efavirenz: Decreases progesterone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Finererone: Progesterone increases finererone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor serum potassium and adjust finererone dosage as needed. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Progesterone increases levels of these drugs via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone: Increases progesterone levels via time-dependent CYP3A inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline: Increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Letermovir and Levoketoconazole: Increase progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Lomitapide: Progesterone increases lomitapide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Do not exceed a lomitapide dose of 30 mg/day. 4. Minor Interactions: Acetazolamide and Anastrozole: Increase progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. Cyclophosphamide: Increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. Doxorubicin and Doxorubicin Liposomal: Progesterone increases the toxicity of these drugs, potentially enhancing neutropenia. The clinical significance is unknown. Drospirenone: Increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. Larotrectinib: Increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. Ribociclib: Increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. Ruxolitinib and Ruxolitinib Topical: Progesterone increases the levels of these drugs via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 5. Pharmacodynamic Synergism: Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens and Vaginal Conjugated Estrogens: When combined with progesterone, these may cause breast tenderness. The clinical significance is unknown. 6. Recommendations for Contraception: Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised when using drugs that interact with natural progesterone to avoid reduced efficacy or increased toxicity. This detailed explanation provides a comprehensive understanding of the interactions, dosing, and monitoring requirements for natural progesterone.
